items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: being Mel Lewis one of them, they used that China cymbal for that low frequency

ctx.x: I’m going to come back to that because it makes me think of the “Straight Ahead from Havana” that you sent. I wanted to ask, some bandleaders, I think most famously Count Basie, was known for not saying much to his musicians unless they really were behaving badly or playing badly. And I wonder if Dizzy spoke to you about what he wanted?

Well yes he did. Dizzy was the type, Dizzy, my dear friend, my father, my brother, Dizzy Gillespie was famous in the business for being a pain in the neck for drummers. He was © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

hard on drummers. So but Dizzy, aside from teaching me a lot about the bebop vocabulary, which I really appreciate because he did just not talk to me about what he wanted me to play in his band, he taught me, it was a daily lesson about bebop vocabulary, about jazz, about life. Yeah.
